title: Tour the instrument
spec: U00 · MedFlow Copilot, screen by screen
intro: Your classroom is an app, not a page. Six stops: the review queue, the Copilot panel, the toggle bar, the token receipt, the Compare drawer, and the stamp that decides whether any of it counted.
foot: Do it for real: SETUP.md — two terminals, no API key — then localhost:5173

steps.title: Stop 1 — the review queue
narrative: MedFlow Copilot is a prior-authorization portal. The left rail is the clinician's app: Review queue, Requests, Members, Submit request. The queue itself holds three requests that scored between the review and approval thresholds, so a human has to decide: PA-1002 (score 65, missing a neurological deficit), PA-1004 (65, failed 12 weeks conservative management), PA-1010 (50, two criteria missing).

Learn these three ids now. They are the cast for fifteen modules — almost every graded question in the course is about one of them, and you will watch strategies get them right, get them expensively right, and occasionally get them wrong.
steps.youDo: Start both terminals from SETUP.md, open localhost:5173, and leave it running beside this player for the whole course.

before.title: WORK QUEUE — three requests awaiting a clinician

views.text: Left: the queue. Right: the Copilot panel — every call gets a receipt. That header line is the whole design of the app.

steps.title: Stop 2 — the toggle bar is your table of contents
narrative: The Copilot panel has three controls and no settings menu. The toggle bar picks the context strategy — ten of them, naive through routed. The standing questions dropdown picks a preset. The box under it takes free-form questions.

Two rules that will save you an hour of confusion. The ten toggles map one-to-one onto modules — notes is U03, okf is U05, isolated is U09, routed is U12 — so treat the bar as a syllabus. And only the preset questions are graded: a free-form ask comes back stamped UNGRADED and proves nothing, however good the answer looks.
steps.youDo: Click each toggle once to see the bar highlight move, then open the standing-questions dropdown and read all ten presets.

steps.title: Stop 3 — the receipt, line by line
narrative: Pick Q1 — "Which criteria apply to procedure 72148 and what is the weight of each?" — leave the mode on naive, and press Ask. Under the answer, the Token Lens prints an itemized bill for that one call.

Read it as five lines, because each line is a course track. System 65 — the static surface, U06. Retrieved 1,612 — the whole seeded domain, dumped in; selection, U04–U05. Tool results 0 — shaping, U07. History 0 — memory, U03 and U08. User turn 17 — the only part most people call "the prompt". They sum to 1,694, and that reconciliation always holds: five layers, one total, no unexplained remainder.
steps.youDo: Ask Q1 in naive, then add the five layer numbers on the receipt by hand and check they equal the input total.
steps.claudeSays: The model read all 1,612 tokens of dumped records, found the three criteria for 72148, and reported them with their weights. Every other record in the dump was paid for and ignored.

view.question: Q1 · criteria and weights for procedure 72148

steps.title: Stop 4 — one toggle, same verdict
narrative: Now flip the bar to okf and press Ask again. Same question, same answer text, same green stamp — and the retrieved layer falls from 1,612 to 280, because instead of a domain dump the assembler shipped two canonical concept files plus the procedure catalog.

Watch the session strip along the bottom while you do it. It read 1 call · 1,694 in-tok · $0.0058; after the second ask it reads 2 calls · 2,056 in-tok · $0.0077. That strip accumulates for as long as the app stays open, and several labs later in the course are built on reading it.
steps.youDo: With Q1 still pinned, click okf and Ask. Compare the retrieved line, then glance at the session strip at the bottom of the panel.

steps.title: Stop 5 — the Compare drawer
narrative: Clicking Compare strategies puts two receipts side by side for the same question and does the arithmetic for you: okf used 79% fewer input tokens than naive · cost Δ $0.0040 saved. Both stamped VERIFIED.

This drawer is where most of the course's evidence gets produced — U04 compares naive against jit here, U07 compares budgeted against compressed. Get used to reading the two receipts and the two stamps, because the drawer will happily show you a cheaper column that failed its answer key.
steps.youDo: Click Compare strategies, set the left column to naive and the right to okf, and read the summary bar at the bottom of the drawer.

steps.title: Stop 6 — the stamp is the point
narrative: One more screen before you start: Members. Member M-2003's date of birth carries a REDACTED badge, because the seed data minimizes that field on purpose. Now ask Q7 — "What is member M-2003's date of birth?" — in naive.

Naive dumps the whole domain, the model finds something that looks like a birth date, and answers "born on 1984-06-17 according to the member record". The grader stamps ✕ FAILED: the key required a refusal and forbade a date pattern. The control arm — the one that spends the most and hides nothing — is the arm that fabricates. Nine of its ten answers are correct; this is the tenth.

That is the law the app exists to enforce, and the only thing you need to carry into U01: a token saving that fails its answer key is not a saving — and a token expense that fails it is just a more expensive defect.
steps.youDo: Open Members, find the REDACTED badge on M-2003, then ask Q7 in naive and read the stamp.

after.title: THE CONTROL ARM FAILS ITS OWN KEY
